title: Certainty and brashness with reviewed content/style pools
context: A manager recommends a pilot of flexible working arrangements to employees. Vary epistemic certainty and interpersonal brashness independently while preserving the policy and supporting points.

dimensions.name: Epistemic certainty
dimensions.definition: The strength of the speaker's expressed confidence in the truth of the recommendation's supporting claims, holding the underlying evidence constant.
dimensions.low_anchor: Tentative confidence; acknowledges that the conclusion may be mistaken.
dimensions.high_anchor: Firm confidence in the conclusion, without claiming new evidence or dismissing other people.

levels.instruction: Express tentative confidence in the recommendation and its supporting inferences.
Express firm confidence in the recommendation and its supporting inferences.

dimensions.name: Interpersonal brashness
dimensions.definition: How presumptuous and dismissive of alternative views the speaker sounds, distinct from confidence in whether the claims are true.
dimensions.low_anchor: Modest and open to other views, regardless of the certainty of the claims.
dimensions.high_anchor: Presumptuous and dismissive of alternative views, regardless of the certainty of the claims.

levels.instruction: Use a modest and open interpersonal stance without changing the assigned epistemic certainty.
Use a presumptuous and dismissive interpersonal stance without changing the assigned epistemic certainty.

dimensions.name: Substantive argument strength
dimensions.definition: The amount and relevance of substantive support for the policy, excluding the speaker's confidence and interpersonal manner.
dimensions.hold_constant: Retain the same substantive supporting points and their scope; do not add evidence, facts, or claims to intensify the assigned perspectives.

dimensions.name: Expected persuasion
dimensions.definition: A model judge's expectation of how compelling the recommendation might be to employees. This is diagnostic, not a participant outcome.
dimensions.low_anchor: Expected to be unpersuasive to the stated audience.
dimensions.high_anchor: Expected to be persuasive to the stated audience.

candidate_review.rationale: For this illustrative factorial design, distinguish confidence in the claims from the interpersonal stance by manipulating both independently.
Adding substantive support would change more than the assigned certainty or interpersonal stance.
Persuasion is the response of interest and should not be suppressed or used to select messages. Model expectations do not constitute behavioral evidence.

blueprints.context: Write an internal message from a manager recommending a voluntary two-day-per-week remote-work pilot. The scenario is hypothetical.
required_content: Recommend a voluntary pilot allowing two remote days per week.
The pilot would let employees reduce commuting on those days.
Teams would arrange their shared office days to preserve opportunities for in-person coordination.
Recommend evaluating the pilot before deciding whether to continue it.

content_pool: Explain how two remote days could reduce the need to commute on those days.
Explain how teams could use shared office days for in-person coordination.
Explain how a voluntary pilot would allow employees to decide whether to participate.
Explain how evaluating the pilot could inform a later decision about continuing it.
Explain how trying a pilot allows the organization to revisit its arrangement.
Explain how combining remote days and shared office days could address different work needs.
style_pool: State the recommendation first and then explain the supporting reasons.
Open with an everyday example before presenting the recommendation.
Organize the message around a question about how the pilot would work.
Compare the proposed pilot with the current arrangement before stating the recommendation.

example_notice: Hypothetical starting specification with hand-written pool suggestions, not model-generated or human-validated materials. Review all content, styles, and thresholds before generation.
